definitions.explanation: The raised platform on which an orchestra conductor stands during a performance or rehearsal. Elevates the conductor so that all musicians can see the baton and gestures clearly.

examples.japanese: {指揮者|しきしゃ}が{指揮|しき}{台|だい}に{立|た}った。
examples.english: The conductor stepped onto the podium.

examples.japanese: {指揮|しき}{台|だい}の{上|うえ}から{全体|ぜんたい}を{見渡|みわた}して{指示|しじ}を{出|だ}す。
examples.english: From atop the podium, the conductor surveys the ensemble and gives directions.

examples.japanese: {新|あたら}しい{音楽|おんがく}{監督|かんとく}が{初|はじ}めて{指揮|しき}{台|だい}に{上|あ}がり、{拍手|はくしゅ}で{迎|むか}えられた。
examples.english: The new music director stepped onto the podium for the first time and was greeted with applause.

notes:
A compound of {指揮|しき} (conducting, command) and {台|だい} (stand, platform). The podium is a symbol of the conductor's authority and is central to the concert stage layout.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {指揮|しき}{台|だい}に{立|た}つ: to stand on the podium
- {指揮|しき}{台|だい}に{上|あ}がる: to step up to the podium
- {指揮|しき}{台|だい}を{降|お}りる: to step down from the podium
- {指揮|しき}{台|だい}の{前|まえ}: in front of the podium

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {演壇|えんだん}: lecture podium, lectern — the podium used for speeches, not music
- {指揮棒|しきぼう}: baton — the stick the conductor holds
- {指揮者|しきしゃ}: conductor — the person who stands on the podium
